prompt: Inserting 100,000 rows one at a time takes 10 minutes, mostly in per-statement overhead.
why: Batch 1,000 rows per statement and pay the fixed cost 100 times instead of 100,000.
trap: Faster hardware doesn't remove fixed per-call costs.

prompt: Appending to a dynamic array occasionally copies everything into a new block, yet appends are still called O(1).
why: Doubling capacity spreads each copy across many cheap appends: O(1) amortized.
trap: One expensive operation doesn't make the average expensive.

prompt: A logger sends each log line as its own network packet, and the overhead uses more bandwidth than the logs themselves.
tells: each log line as its own network packet
why: Buffer lines and flush in batches so headers are shared across many lines.
trap: Batching adds a little delay; usually a fine trade.

prompt: A client opens a new HTTPS connection for every API call, paying a TLS handshake each time.
tells: new HTTPS connection for every API call
why: Reuse connections (keep-alive) so one handshake covers many calls.
trap: Latency numbers explain the cost; reuse is how you spread it.

prompt: Each request opens a fresh database connection, and connection setup takes longer than the query itself.
tells: setup takes longer than the query
why: A pool pays setup once and spreads it across thousands of queries.
trap: Pool sizing uses Little's law, but the reason to pool is spreading a fixed cost.

prompt: A Java service is slow for its first minute after each deploy, then fast. Deploying 40 times a day makes users notice.
why: JIT warm-up is a one-time cost amortized over the process lifetime; frequent restarts stop it from paying off.
trap: The slow requests show up in the tail, but the cause is an unamortized fixed cost.

prompt: Every CI run reinstalls all dependencies from scratch, though they change about once a month.
why: Cache the install layer: pay it once a month instead of every run.
trap: Speeding the install in parallel helps less than not doing it at all.

prompt: A database flushes to disk on every commit, capping it at a few hundred commits per second. Batching commits arriving within 2 ms into one flush raises throughput tenfold.
tells: flushes to disk on every commit
why: Group commit shares one expensive fsync across many transactions, trading a little latency for throughput.
trap: Latency numbers explain why fsync is costly; the fix is spreading that cost.
